clues: This city sits in the far northwest of the United States, southwest of Seattle. Long arms of the sea reach deep into the land all around it.
Most storms here roll in off cold northern seas, loaded with wet air. They bring long spells of rain, low cloud, and thick fog.
In November 1853, this town was named the capital of the whole territory. It has held that job ever since, the first and only one.
This city hugs the head of a small inlet at the far south end of Puget Sound. That south tip is the end of the sound's long reach inland.
The governor of Washington works in this city. State lawmakers meet here to pass laws for the whole state.
